bands.label: Ceasefire that does not hold
bands.summary: Successive US-brokered truces are announced while Israeli strikes, ground operations, and an Israeli ministerial pledge to stay for years continue across southern Lebanon.

bands.label: Open war and first ceasefire
bands.summary: Israel escalates to full air and ground war against Hezbollah, kills its senior leadership, and signs a first US-mediated ceasefire in late 2024 that frays through 2025 and 2026.

bands.label: Solidarity front with Gaza
bands.summary: After Oct 7, Hezbollah opens daily cross-border fire from south Lebanon and Israel responds, displacing tens of thousands on both sides of the Blue Line.

bands.label: 1701 era and frozen front
bands.summary: The 2006 war ends with UN Security Council Resolution 1701 and a UNIFIL-monitored buffer that is widely seen as unenforced, while Hezbollah grows into Lebanon's dominant armed and political force.

bands.label: Invasion, occupation, resistance
bands.summary: Israel invades Lebanon in 1982, occupies the south for 18 years, Hezbollah forms as an armed resistance, and Israel withdraws in 2000 leaving disputed border points.

frames.label: Oct 2023 cross-border fire
frames.note: The story begins when Hezbollah opened a cross-border front in solidarity with Gaza after Oct 7, 2023, drawing Israeli return fire. Under this frame, the current strikes and disarmament pressure read as the unfinished resolution of a war Hezbollah chose to enter. US, Israeli, and most Western diplomatic readouts open with this start date.

frames.label: 2006 war and UNSCR 1701
frames.note: The story begins with the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war and the UN Security Council Resolution 1701 framework that was supposed to disarm Hezbollah south of the Litani. Under this frame, today's standoff reads as a 20-year failure of an unenforced ceasefire architecture. UN officials, EU diplomats, and Lebanese state institutions tend to open here.

frames.label: 1982 Israeli invasion
frames.note: The story begins with Israel's 1982 invasion of Lebanon and the occupation that birthed Hezbollah as a resistance movement. Under this frame, current strikes and the demand to disarm read as the latest chapter of a four-decade occupation cycle. Hezbollah, Iranian state media, and much of the Lebanese Shia public open with this start date.
